Name: Integrated Tax System
Project Summary: A Comptroller of Maryland initiative to modernize the State’s tax administration by replacing outdated legacy systems with Government Premier, a cloud-based integrated tax system (ITS), designed to enhance efficiency, transparency, and taxpayer services. The program integrates with Maryland’s data warehouse to improve querying, auditing, reporting, and fraud detection. Implementation is progressing through phased releases, with the final phase scheduled for deployment in August 2026.

Name: State Financial Modernization
Project Summary: A Comptroller of Maryland initiative to modernize statewide financial management. This effort, mandated under House Bill 709/Senate Bill 659, establishes the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise (21CFSE) to deliver a centralized ERP for all state agencies. At its core, this initiative includes the replacement of the State's aging Financial Management Information System (FMIS) with a modern, cloud-based Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution. Broadly, this modernization will transform Maryland's financial management infrastructure through business process reengineering, consolidating disparate systems, and improving financial data quality and analysis to enhance fiscal compliance across all state agencies.

Name: CPB Payroll System Modernization (PSM)
Project Summary: A statewide project by the Central Payroll Bureau to replace the legacy mainframe payroll system with a modern, cloud-based Software as a Service (SaaS) solution. This transformation is designed to streamline and automate outdated payroll processes while introducing standardized industry best practices to strengthen efficiency, accuracy, and compliance. The new scalable system will serve over 100,000 employees across all branches of the State of Maryland, modernizing payroll operations and enhancing the user experience.

Name: Capital Budgeting Information System (CBIS) replacement
Project Summary: This project, an extension of the State’s Budget Analysis and Reporting System (BARS), is focused on modernizing the management of capital projects and programs. It will replace the existing CBIS, eliminate manual processes, and introduce advanced capabilities such as facility planning and geospatial integration. The new solution will be fully integrated with BARS and the Financial Management Information System (FMIS) to ensure consistency across budgeting and accounting processes, providing a more efficient, transparent, and secure approach to managing the State’s capital budgeting activities.

Name: Fleet Management System Replacement
Project Summary: A statewide initiative by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to replace the legacy WebFleetMaster system with a fully functional and customizable software solution. The new system will modernize fleet operations by tracking vehicles, repairs, usage, drivers, and telematics data, and consolidating manual processes. It aims to provide enhanced reporting and dashboard capabilities and will interface with critical platforms including FMIS and eMMA. The goal is to deliver a modern, secure, and integrated fleet management solution that supports fiscal accountability.

Name: Maryland Marketplace (eMMA) eProcurement Solution
Project Summary: This project is modernizing the State of Maryland’s enterprise procurement platform to standardize how State agencies manage solicitations, contracts, and vendor interactions. Following an internal assessment and an Executive Order, the eMMA platform is enhancing its capabilities with strategic sourcing, catalog management, advanced reporting, and improved compliance for small and minority-owned businesses. The goal is to unify procurement practices, increase accountability and transparency, and drive efficiency, equity, and innovation in Maryland’s procurement operations.

Name: AS400 Replacement
Project Summary: A Department of General Services (DGS) initiative to replace the outdated AS400 system with a secure, cloud-based Construction Project Management Information System (PMIS). The PMIS will streamline how approximately 20 State agencies plan, manage, and report on capital and maintenance projects. It is designed to reduce manual processes, eliminate redundant data entry, and expand reporting capabilities. The new system will integrate with other state systems and enable more effective collaboration and decision-making for managing public assets and investments.

Name: Energy Efficiency Program Management System
Agency: Department of Housing and Community Development
Project Summary: A strategic modernization project by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to replace the existing system supporting the Housing and Building Energy Programs. It will deploy a Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solution to provide robust program management capabilities, including application intake, invoicing, reporting, energy audits, and financial tracking. The goal is to strengthen operational efficiency, streamline program delivery, reduce costs, and improve service responsiveness for residents, aligning with State objectives to expand access to energy efficiency programs.

Name: Juvenile Case Management Modernization
Project Summary: The Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) is seeking an IT solution to replace its legacy case management application, ASSIST (developed in 1999), due to significant limitations in scalability, security, and maintainability. The new system, either a comprehensive modernization or a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution, must support current security standards, offer scalability, and allow for future enhancements. It is also required to interface seamlessly with the MD Benefits CJAMS application to ensure compliance with federal funding and reporting standards (Title IV-E).

Name: DNR Modernization and OneStop Integration Project
Project Summary: A statewide initiative by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to replace the COMPASS system with a modern, web-based Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) platform for comprehensive licensing and permitting services. The solution will provide a central point of access for all 134 licenses and permits, with features including online payment processing, workflow automation, and an Open Application Programming Interface (API) for integration. The project also incorporates Geographic Information System (GIS) enhancements, aiming to improve the customer experience and ensure a scalable system.

Name: Park Reservation and Revenue Management System (PRRMS)
Project Summary: A modernization effort by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to transform park reservations, revenue management, and customer services statewide. The initiative will implement a secure, web-based platform with mobile functionality for efficiently managing reservations for various park facilities (campsites, cabins, etc.). Beyond reservations, the system will integrate modules for retail, gift cards, revenue tracking, and enhanced inventory control. A critical element is the Open Application Programming Interface (API) for future integration, such as with the OneStop portal. Additional scope includes park internet upgrades and a robust GIS system for mapping and wayfinding.

Name: Enterprise Solutions Planning Initiative (ESPI)
Project Summary: A strategic effort led by the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to centralize the planning process for evaluating Major IT Development Project (MITDP) requests. It shifts from siloed, agency-specific planning to a coordinated enterprise-level approach, enabling DoIT to assess requests against existing initiatives or new enterprise projects. ESPI fosters collaboration, identifies common needs, and supports enterprise-wide strategies to optimize resources and align with technology standards. This approach replaces large, upfront planning documents with agile, iterative strategies to strengthen portfolio management and dashboard reporting capabilities.

Name: Maryland OneStop Portal
Project Summary: A statewide initiative to modernize and streamline manual government processes by converting over a thousand paper-based forms and licenses into fully electronic formats. The project addresses the inefficiencies of the current environment, which include duplicative licensing processes, increased administrative costs, and inconsistent service quality. By introducing electronic forms accessible via computer, mobile phone, or tablet, the project will reduce costs, increase efficiency, and deliver a more consistent customer experience. This transformation automates state processes, improving operational performance and supporting Maryland’s vision for digital government.

Name: NwMD Modernization
Project Summary: The Network Maryland Infrastructure Modernization project is a statewide initiative to expand high-speed internet capacity and redundancy from the backbone to county Points of Presence (PoPs). This is necessary as the existing network, designed over 15 years ago, is no longer adequate for the exponential bandwidth demands of Executive Branch agencies. By extending 100-gigabit per second capacity to the county PoPs, the project will improve network performance, strengthen reliability, and enable agencies to adopt and expand cloud-based strategies, meeting current and future technology demands.

Name: Maryland Enterprise Web Strategy
Project Summary: A statewide effort to modernize and consolidate over 100 government websites into a centralized, accessible, secure, user-centered, and cost-effective Content Management System (CMS). The project directly aligns with the Governor’s Executive Order to Transform Maryland Executive Branch Digital Services. It addresses urgent challenges, including compliance with updated ADA Title II requirements, growing security risks from unsupported platforms, and inconsistent user experiences. By consolidating and modernizing digital services, MEWS will create a more accessible, secure, and cost-effective statewide web ecosystem for all residents and employers.

Name: Computerized Criminal History (CCH) Replacement (Phase II)
Agency: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
Project Summary: A modernization initiative by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) to replace the outdated mainframe Computerized Criminal History (CCH) system with a modern, scalable platform. The project aims to enhance the accuracy and timeliness of offender information for law enforcement and other stakeholders by streamlining workflows, automating manual processes, and eliminating duplicative activities. The new platform will conform to national data standards, improve information sharing across agencies, and introduce configurable administrative controls and automated monitoring tools to increase efficiency, reliability, and security in managing criminal history records.

Name: Electronic Patient Health Record (EPHR) Replacement
Agency: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
Project Summary: A DPSCS initiative to implement a fully customized correctional healthcare cloud-based Electronic Patient Health Record (EPHR) system. The solution is designed to improve clinical and operational efficiency by integrating key capabilities such as automated Electronic Medication Administration Records (EMAR) and scheduling, while interfacing with internal and external platforms within the agency. The project aims to replace outdated technology to ensure compliance with rigorous security and privacy standards. The scalable system will enhance care coordination, strengthen operational workflows, and support future growth, delivering a reliable and adaptable solution for correctional healthcare delivery.

Name: Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) Modernization Program
Project Summary: A strategic initiative to transform the delivery of licensing, certification, permitting, and related agricultural services by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA), focusing on Nutrient Management, State Chemist, and Turf and Seed departments. The project will replace outdated systems with a single, streamlined solution, digitize paper-based forms, and introduce secure online payment capabilities. It involves retiring legacy applications and consolidating disparate platforms to reduce redundancy and improve operational efficiency. By providing modern digital services and user-friendly public access, MODP aims to enhance service delivery, improve transparency, and strengthen support for Maryland’s agricultural community.

Name: MDA Digitization and Modernization Project
Project Summary: A statewide initiative to implement a comprehensive, scalable Salesforce-based solution to unify program and grant management across the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). It consolidates licensing, permitting, inspection, enforcement, and grant processes for multiple programs, including Resource Conservation and Plant Industries, onto a single platform. The solution will feature an internal dashboard for real-time visibility into applications and grants, centralized application management, and streamlined communications. Additional features include automated fee management, scheduling for inspections, and business intelligence capabilities. This modernized system aims to reduce administrative burden, improve transparency and regulatory compliance, and increase overall efficiency and responsiveness across MDA operations.

Name: MDE Portal Project
Project Summary: A modernization initiative by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to create a centralized online portal and payment system for managing permitting and licensing applications, replacing primarily paper-based processes. The portal will streamline public access to approximately 460 forms by offering structured informational pages, real-time status tracking, and integrated payment functionality. Key features include a comprehensive payment portal and support for specialized forms like the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) submissions. The goal is to enhance customer service and provide a secure, user-friendly, and fully digital solution for residents and businesses needing timely and accurate environmental permitting.

Name: Wells and Septic Portal
Project Summary: An MDE modernization initiative to streamline the management of on-site sewage disposal systems and well installation permits. It will deliver a comprehensive online platform enabling applicants to submit and pay for permit requests and providing automated application management tools. By digitizing the process, the portal will offer contractors and stakeholders real-time visibility into status updates, reducing delays and improving transparency. The initiative also includes informational web pages and training materials to support public awareness and effective user adoption. This effort is designed to meet all regulatory and operational requirements while enhancing efficiency, accessibility, and accountability in managing Maryland’s well and septic permitting processes.

Name: Environment (MDE) ETS and LRCA System Consolidation and Modernization Project
Project Summary: A strategic initiative to merge and modernize MDE's fragmented legacy IT systems, including the Environmental Tracking System (ETS) and Lead Rental Certification and Accreditation (LRCA) systems, to ensure continued support for regulatory changes, efficiency, and security. This effort aims to streamline operations, reduce costs, and improve MDE's ability to respond to legislative changes. The consolidation covers numerous applications across various programs, such as Water Supply and Air Quality Compliance, for functions like licensing, certification, compliance, and reporting, ultimately seeking to replace outdated technology and provide superior customer experiences.

Name: Statewide Electronic Health Records (EHR) system
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative to replace the legacy Health Management Information System with a commercially available, cloud-based Software as a Service (SaaS) solution. The system will support health and revenue-cycle operations across eleven State-run treatment centers, including eight behavioral health facilities and three hospitals. It will streamline patient admission, discharge, and transfer, and manage functions like revenue cycle, pharmacy, laboratory, and clinical documentation on a standardized platform. Adopting a commercial SaaS product ensures scalability and sustainability, with the goal of enhancing reporting, improving operational efficiency, and ultimately elevating the quality of patient care.

Name: Enterprise Licensing and Regulatory Management Solution (LRMS)
Project Summary: An MDH initiative to enhance the ability of the Maryland Board of Nursing (MBON) to manage health profession services and regulatory functions. It establishes a modern, scalable enterprise platform that will first support the MBON and then be extended to the State’s twenty-two other health profession boards. The solution strengthens public health and safety by enabling more effective credentialing, permitting, licensing, examination, inspection, and discipline of healthcare providers and facilities. By providing a consistent and scalable system, the project advances Maryland’s ability to regulate health professions with greater efficiency, accountability, and transparency.

Name: Integrated Electronic Vital Records Registration System
Project Summary: A statewide MDH initiative to consolidate and modernize legacy applications for managing the creation, retention, and distribution of vital demographic information (e.g., birth, death, marriage certificates). Administered by the Division of Vital Records, Maryland customized the California Integrated Vital Records System (Cal-IVRS) to create a secure, web-based platform that incorporates all legacy data and supports user accounts at medical and funeral facilities. The new system enables streamlined integration with federal partners like the National Center for Health Statistics. The project enhances service delivery, improves operational efficiency, and strengthens data integrity for public health and administrative functions.

Name: Migrate MDH HQ Data Center to the Cloud
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative established in 2020 to strengthen cybersecurity, modernize IT infrastructure, and prepare for the headquarters relocation. The project focuses on migrating servers, applications, and databases from MDH headquarters to a secure, consolidated commercial private cloud facility. Core objectives include implementing enhanced security, establishing a high-availability backup site for continuity of operations and disaster recovery, and later evaluating a transition of select health services to public cloud environments for secure citizen access. In FY22, the scope expanded to include modernizing MDH’s public websites and migrating hosting to the Department of Information Technology (DoIT).

Name: Bed Registry and Referral System
Project Summary: A joint initiative by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) to modernize the tracking and management of behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment capacity. The project implements a commercial off-the-shelf solution configured to MDH specifications, providing real-time visibility into available beds across public and community-based healthcare providers. By facilitating rapid data sharing and timely referrals, the system, which includes a Care Traffic Control System, will improve access to critical services. It will also strengthen reporting capabilities to enhance crisis management, helping MDH and BHA allocate resources more effectively.

Name: MD AIDS Drug Assistance Program (MADAP)
Project Summary: A statewide initiative led by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to modernize and streamline case management services for vulnerable populations. Launched in 2023, the project delivers a secure, cloud-based platform supporting the Maryland Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome Drug Assistance Program and the Chronic Health Impaired Students Program. This new system replaces outdated processes with an integrated approach to enhance efficiency, ensure data security, and improve service delivery for individuals living with AIDS and students with chronic health conditions who rely on government assistance. The effort supports MDH’s mission to improve health outcomes and promote equitable access to care.

Name: OPER to Systems Integration and Modernization
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative to modernize licensing, compliance, and workforce regulatory functions led by the Office of Controlled Substances Administration. The project aims to enhance healthcare delivery and streamline regulatory oversight by replacing outdated manual processes with a unified, cloud-based system accessible to the public. Key benefits include strengthened data security, real-time reporting, disaster recovery, and improved efficiency and adaptability to statutory changes. It supports automated licensing and compliance for Controlled Dangerous Substances, as well as the recruitment, accreditation, and certification of Community Health Workers.

Name: MDH Non-Medicaid Case Management (CMM) Modernization
Project Summary: A strategic initiative by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to implement a modernized case management system for multiple non-Medicaid business units. The project is designed to streamline case management activities by providing a unified interface, standardizing workflows, and enabling efficient data sharing related to service delivery. By consolidating customer information onto a single platform, the solution will improve coordination and reduce redundancies. Salesforce has been selected as the core technology platform, which is expected to enhance operational efficiency, reduce the overall cost of ownership, and provide greater effectiveness and scalability in managing non-Medicaid services.

Name: PHS Data Modernization Program
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) statewide initiative to transform how Public Health Services (PHS) information is collected, managed, and shared. The project will deliver an enterprise platform supporting surveillance data, maternal health, newborn screening, and vital statistics. Through a unified portal, users will gain access to query-based data visualizations, dashboards, and advanced analytics to enhance service planning. The solution is being developed in phases, with the ultimate goal of integrating all public health datasets into a single, secure, and reliable enterprise system to improve transparency, efficiency, and accessibility of health information, positioning the agency to better meet current and future public health needs.

Name: MMT to Behavioral Health ASO (BHASO)
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to secure a vendor to oversee the delivery and management of Medicaid behavioral health services. The selected vendor will serve as the Behavioral Health Administrative Services Organization (BHASO), responsible for implementing and operating a software system to review, process, and pay claims for all Medicaid behavioral health providers. Beyond technology, the vendor must provide deep expertise to ensure the program is administered in alignment with State and federal requirements, aiming to streamline service administration, reduce operational risk, and improve access and accountability.

Name: MMT to Business Process Reengineering & Consolidated CRM
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative to procure and implement a new Software as a Service (SaaS) solution to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of case managers and supervisors through Business Process Reengineering (BPR) and Consolidated Case Management Modernization. The system will introduce automated workflow management, alerts, and triggers to streamline daily responsibilities and strengthen provider customer relationship management. It will initially interface with the existing Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS) before integrating with the new Maryland Modular Medicaid Management Information System (MMT), aiming to improve service delivery, enhance provider relationships, and reduce reliance on paper-based processes and support a more modern and responsive operational environment.

Name: MMT to Consolidated Call Center and IVR
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) Consolidated Call Center (CCC) and IVR project is to unify the agency’s multiple direct-dial call centers into a single, centralized operation. The project focuses on modernizing technology platforms, standardizing workflows, and optimizing processes to improve efficiency and service delivery. By establishing CCC and IVR, MDH aims to streamline operations, reduce duplication, and provide residents with more consistent and accessible support across health programs and services. A key priority is implementing solutions that comply with the Department of Information Technology’s (DoIT) security standards, enhancing customer experience and operational performance.

Name: MMT to CMS Interoperability Rule
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to implement the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Interoperability and Patient Access final rule. The project requires the Maryland Medicaid Administration to adopt Health Level Seven (HL7) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), enabling the secure exchange of health data and streamlining prior authorizations. It also mandates operational changes, such as processing standard prior authorization requests within seven days. The goal is to improve patient and provider access to health data, enhance system integration, reduce administrative burden, improve care coordination, and lower costs.

Name: MMT to Dental Administrative Services (DASO)
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to improve access to dental care for Medicaid members and ensure prompt reimbursement for providers by establishing a new Dental Administrative Services Organization (DASO). The project's dual objectives are to increase annual utilization of preventive and restorative dental services by at least one percent each year, and to develop and operate a robust claims processing system that ensures accuracy and timeliness. The system is required to process electronic claims within 14 calendar days, enhancing the oral health outcomes of Medicaid members while modernizing and streamlining the administration of dental services.

Name: MMT to Decision Support & Enterprise Data Warehouse
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to establish a centralized platform, or Data Lake, for storing and analyzing critical health data currently dispersed across multiple systems. The secure, cloud-based environment will aggregate data sources, including claims, authorizations, and recipient/provider information from various Medicaid systems (MMIS, BHASO, DASO, UCA). This effort is essential for meeting the CMS Interoperability Rule by providing data securely through APIs. Consolidating data will improve reporting, enhance analytic capabilities, and enable more informed decision-making across programs.

Name: MMT to EDI Gateway
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to modernize how healthcare data is exchanged via Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) between providers, Medicare, other health plans, and third-party clearinghouses. The project aims to streamline the transfer of information, reducing processing time and improving the accuracy of data exchanges. By transitioning to a more scalable and secure environment, the project will strengthen system reliability, reduce operational risks, and ensure the long-term sustainability of electronic data interchange capabilities in support of Maryland’s healthcare ecosystem.

Name: MMT to Enterprise Document Management System
Project Summary: The Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) Enterprise Document Management System (EDMS) project is to implement a comprehensive enterprise-wide solution to automate the organization, digitization, secure storage, and classification of documents across all Medicaid business areas. Its primary goal is to improve operational efficiency by establishing a centralized, authoritative repository for critical documents. The Core features include automated ingestion, indexing, classification, version control, role-based access, and secure audit trails. By enabling controlled document editing and sharing, the system will strengthen collaboration, streamline business workflows, and safeguard the integrity of Medicaid data while meeting compliance requirements and enhancing its ability to respond quickly to programmatic and operational needs.

Name: MMT to Hospice And Maryland Daycare Enrollment
Project Summary: The Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) Hospice and Medical Daycare Enrollment project is a modernization initiative designed to resolve longstanding data conflicts in the Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS) that occur when beneficiaries transition between long-term care, hospice, or medical daycare programs. The project will integrate hospice and medical daycare programs into the State’s Eligibility and Enrollment (E&E) application, automating processes and accelerating payment timeliness to nursing facilities. It will also deliver enhanced reporting dashboards and automate the Form 257 process for short-term stays, ultimately consolidating these improvements into a single customer relationship management platform to streamline workflows and ensure a more reliable, integrated solution for both providers and beneficiaries.

Name: MMT to MES Claims Module
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to modernize and replace the legacy system used to process Medicaid claims, aligning with MITA 3.0 principles. The new system will streamline operations by consolidating processing for Mental Hygiene, Developmental Disabilities, and Dental claims, reducing duplicate work and improving accuracy. It will incorporate advanced features like imaging, workflow management, and a robust business rules engine for adaptable benefit plans. The solution will also strengthen critical functions, including coordination of benefits, surveillance and utilization review, and federal/State reporting across a wide range of benefit programs.

Name: MMT to Non Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT)
Project Summary: The Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) is a Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative to acquire and implement a comprehensive technology solution to modernize the management of Medicaid transportation services. The system is being procured to function as the central platform for dispatching, scheduling, and processing claims. By consolidating all program functions into a single solution, the project aims to improve service delivery for beneficiaries, increase efficiency for providers, and ensure rigorous compliance with federal and State regulations. This strategic investment strengthens Maryland’s Medicaid program infrastructure to better support residents’ access to essential healthcare.

Name: MMT to Provider Management Module
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to streamline provider enrollment, updates, and revalidation across Medicaid Fee for Service, Behavioral Health, and Pharmacy programs. The project aims to modernize provider management processes by building a comprehensive system that supports efficient functions and regulatory compliance. It includes acquiring Help Desk and application processing resources, implementing an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system to improve provider communications, and developing a robust reporting platform for tracking operational data. These efforts are intended to enhance service delivery, improve data accuracy, and strengthen overall program administration for Maryland’s healthcare providers.

Name: MMT to Surveillance Utilization Review Subsystem
Project Summary: The Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) Surveillance and Utilization Review System (SURS) Replacement project is a Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative to implement a comprehensive, modernized solution that enhances oversight and program integrity by replacing the outdated SURS. The project is designed to streamline and consolidate manual processes and retire legacy applications that no longer meet operational or compliance needs. By deploying this replacement system, MDH will strengthen its ability to meet federal audit requirements and ensure continued compliance with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) program integrity mandate, ultimately improving efficiency, accuracy, and accountability in managing health program data and supporting the department’s long-term compliance and operational objectives..

Name: MMT to Utilization Control Agent (UCA)
Project Summary: A Maryland Department of Health (MDH) initiative under the Medicaid Enterprise Systems Modular Transformation (MMT) to strengthen oversight of medical services reimbursed by Maryland Medicaid through a contracted Utilization Control Agent (UCA). The agent evaluates the necessity and appropriateness of services across hospitals, nursing facilities, and community-based care programs. The UCA authorizes hospital inpatient services only when outpatient delivery is not effective and approves long-term care/community-based services only when individuals meet medical eligibility criteria. A critical responsibility is to identify, monitor, and report potential misuse or inappropriate utilization, promoting higher standards of care and safeguarding taxpayer resources.

Name: Electronic Licensing Modernization (ELMo)
Project Summary: A statewide initiative led by the Department of Labor to replace its legacy licensing system with a modern, cloud-based Platform as a Service (PaaS) solution, leveraging a proof of concept with Salesforce Public Sector Solutions. The project is designed to enhance the customer experience for applicants and licensees while improving internal efficiency through streamlined office procedures. Key features include configurable workflows, enhanced online services, improved payment processing, electronic content management, mobile access, and an integrated analytics platform. Delivery is planned iteratively, starting with a pilot in Q3 FY26, to standardize licensing patterns across the State.

Name: LABOR Omni-channel Contact Center System (LOCCS)
Project Summary: A multi-phase initiative by the Maryland Department of Labor's Unemployment Insurance division to modernize and centralize contact center operations. It replaces the temporary, outsourced COVID-era call center with a State-managed, cloud-based Software as a Service (SaaS) solution. LOCCS provides omni-channel capabilities, including voice, chat, email, and self-service IVR. The solution is designed to improve customer service, streamline case handling, reduce duplicate data entry, and integrate with the existing BEACON and Salesforce platforms to deliver a modern, efficient, and resident-focused customer service model across unemployment insurance functions.

Name: Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)
Project Summary: FAMLI's digital platform is an end-to-end system to operate Maryland's paid family and medical leave insurance program. It will provide secure online services for workers to apply for benefits, submit documentation, and track payments. Concurrently, it enables employers to manage accounts and remit required contributions. For State operations, it supports staff workflows for claims, appeals, customer service, and compliance, with automation and program-integrity controls to reduce improper payments. The platform, which will integrate with a banking partner for payment issuance, is sized to serve 2.6 million covered workers and over 180,000 employers.

Name: New Unified Financial Aid System for Higher Education ( or MDCAPS 2.0)
Project Summary: A statewide initiative by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to transform student access to financial aid across 29 State programs. The project implements a new web-based application that consolidates access to all scholarships, offering features like multilingual support, mobile accessibility, and electronic signatures. The system will streamline administrative functions, including processing applications, managing awards, and verifying eligibility. It aims to improve the student experience, enhance communication with real-time updates, and strengthen data-driven decision making through detailed reports and performance metrics.

Name: MIA's Insurance Tracking System (ITS)
Project Summary: This project is replacing the Maryland Insurance Administration’s (MIA) outdated, custom-built Enterprise System (ES) from the 1990s with the Insurance Tracking System (ITS), which leverages the Salesforce platform. The goal is to automate and digitize MIA processes for improved functionality, efficiency, and security across business units like Company Licensing, Fraud and Enforcement, and Hearings and Orders. The project includes introducing case and document management, a centralized database, and new portals for communication with the public and licensees to remove data silos and strengthen governance and risk management controls.

Name: CCATS Migration Project
Project Summary: A Maryland State Department of Education modernization initiative to migrate the licensing and scholarship components of the Child Care Administration Tracking System (CCATS) to Salesforce, a secure, cloud-based solution. CCATS is a centralized tool managing early care and education programs, including facility licensing, the Child Care Scholarship Program, and workforce data. The transition enables a full system redesign to streamline customer service, accelerate payment processing for providers, and strengthen accountability for quality care. The new platform will also enhance data accuracy and simplify code maintenance to more efficiently adapt to evolving regulations.

Name: MSDE Website
Project Summary: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is designing and building a new primary website to replace the existing unsecured and unsupported SharePoint 2013 CMS. The new website must be modern, intuitive, and built with a fully responsive and accessible web design to meet the agency's functional and technical requirements, aligning with a new strategic plan for public education. The project includes requirements for hosting services, UX strategy, information architecture, content strategy, and ongoing support, with MSDE seeking a cost-effective solution that aligns with the State's digital standards, potentially leveraging the DoIT-led effort to standardize on Drupal CMS.

Name: Automated Licensing and Registration Tracking System (ALRTS)
Project Summary: A Maryland State Police (MSP), The Automated Licensing and Registration Tracking System (ALRTS) project initiative is to modernize and streamline the State’s regulated firearms licensing and registration processes through a fully automated, web-based portal. Mandated by the Firearm Safety Act, it replaces outdated manual and paper-based applications, eliminating reliance on the legacy Lotus Domino-based platform. The system allows citizens, dealers, and agencies to electronically submit applications (like the 77R for firearm purchases) and track status in real-time. By consolidating these functions, ALRTS reduces application processing time, improves reporting and metrics, and enhances operational efficiency for the MSP Licensing Division, firearm dealers, and handgun instructors.

Name: Campaign Reporting Information System (CRIS)
Project Summary: The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) is procuring a new Campaign Reporting Information System (NCRIS) prior to the 2026 election cycle to fully manage the State’s campaign finance system. The system enables contributors and committees to self-register, document all financial activity (contributions, expenditures, loans), and electronically file reports. The SBE uses the system (currently MDCRIS) to oversee filing cycles, approve registrations, run audits on delinquent committees, and fine them. It also includes the Business Contribution Disclosure System (BCDS) module for required electronic filing of contribution disclosures by persons doing business with the State.

Name: 2026 New Voting System
Project Summary: The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) is procuring a new statewide voting system to replace the current leased system, which expires in March 2027. The new system must be certified by both the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) under VVSG and the SBE. Procurement must be initiated in 2025 to allow sufficient time for the RFP process, evaluation, state certification, and implementation before the 2028 Presidential Election. The SBE is requesting proposals for both purchase and lease options, with the Voting System Division responsible for the project's procurement, implementation, and operations.

Name: Statewide Pollbook Modernization (SPM)
Project Summary: A Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) initiative to procure and implement a modernized electronic pollbook solution for use by the SBE and local boards during the FY28 statewide election cycle. The project encompasses the acquisition of new pollbook hardware and software, Maryland-specific system modifications, and comprehensive statewide integration and acceptance testing. It includes training, change management, deployment, and long-term operational support. The scope also covers the decommissioning and disposal of legacy pollbook equipment. The SPM project is designed to provide Maryland with a secure, reliable, and fully supported system to improve election management and strengthen the integrity of the voting process.

Name: Voter Registration and Election Administration Modernization
Project Summary: The State Board of Elections (SBE) project to procure and implement a modernized, Statewide, centralized, GIS-capable, and secure voter registration and election administration solution for the 2030 statewide elections. The anticipated modified off-the-shelf system will replace the 20-year-old MDVOTERS system. The new solution will incorporate a real-time database accessible by at least 500 election officials across Maryland and will handle candidate filing, election judge tracking, petition processes, and ballot production while interfacing with electronic pollbooks.

Name: Computerized Records Information System
Project Summary: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) Cloud Revenue Integrated System Modernization (CRIS) project modernizes and migrates mainframe-based applications, including the tax credit application system and the Maryland Business Entity System (MBES), to a secure cloud platform. The project delivers a Section 508(c) compliant, web-enabled solution accessible on multiple devices and compatible with assistive technologies. This modernization enables secure online submission, status monitoring, and corrections for tax credit applications. It also expands online capabilities for businesses by transitioning manual processes (like filing annual reports and submitting personal property returns) to digital services via the Maryland Business Express portal.

Name: Maryland Assessment Administration and Valuation System (MAAVS) Modernization
Project Summary: A statewide initiative to modernize Maryland’s Computer Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) system, which is responsible for maintaining records and valuing every parcel of land for ad valorem property taxes. The current legacy system suffers from an outdated interface, poor performance during heavy demand, and a lack of mobile functionality. The MAAVS project will implement a modern, reliable, and scalable solution designed to improve system usability, streamline workflows, reduce inefficiencies, and enhance service delivery for staff and taxpayers. By replacing the antiquated system, the project will strengthen Maryland’s ability to perform property assessments with greater accuracy and efficiency.

Name: Financial Systems Modernization
Project Summary: A strategic initiative to transition the State Treasurer’s Office (STO) from its aging IBM AS400/i5 Treasury and Insurance Management System to a modern, cloud-based Microsoft enterprise resource planning (ERP) financial and insurance management solution. This modernization is essential to ensuring the continuity and enhancement of the Treasurer’s Office mission-critical functions, which include funds disbursement, daily cash flow management, reconciliation, ACH/wire transfers, investment of State funds, and claims management. The transition is imperative due to IBM’s end-of-service date for the legacy platform. The FSM project will deliver a secure, reliable, and scalable platform that strengthens financial management and improves efficiency.
